generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a thornless shrub of upright stems carrying big, soft, maple-like leaves and white flowers like crumpled tissue paper. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1.6 m tall at 12 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: bright green leaves; white flowers; red berries later; shredding tan bark. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: soft red thimbleberries, wider than long, some still pale. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) is authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: white flowers in May to July; berries red in July and August. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): shreddy bark peeling on old canes; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.organs.bloom.season.flower_lo.note: Its flowers drawn one by one (spec rework L1b): large white crinkled flowers 3 to 5 cm across with many stamens, 3 to 11 in a cluster, drawn opening together. From general descriptions of the species (OregonFlora, the Flora of North America and nursery and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read). The size is the flower's width, or a closed corolla's length, over the fruit's length, roughly as in life. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): five white petals between five sepals on a floral cup, its stamens by hand and thirty free pistils, from the characters of its own, Rosaceae's and Rubus's by the rules at the flowering plants.

traits.note: Jepson eFlora's account of the species, as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read: pistils more than 30, styles short and thick, ovaries densely hairy; petals 14 to 22 mm, white. Floras say only that the stamens are numerous, so their count stays by hand.

traits.flowering_position.note: FEIS's thimbleberry review (page read): flowers in clusters of 2 to 10 at the ends of the branches, on second-year stems.
